summary: The day lends itself to three one-statement SQL tasks on the desk tables, a rerunnable DROP TABLE IF EXISTS, a DELETE that removes only the duplicate ticket 1, and a SELECT with a column list, WHERE and AS aliases, while its DCL, TCL, overview and interview steps rest on accounts, START TRANSACTION at the client, a naming convention or a spoken answer that sqlite3 in the page cannot show.

steps.title: DDL: statements that shape tables
steps.reason: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS runs unchanged on SQLite 3.39 and MySQL 9.7, and its effect is visible: the table is gone, the other tables keep their rows, and a second run raises nothing. The page names the slips a check catches: a plain DROP fails the second time, and DELETE removes rows but keeps the table; MODIFY, CHANGE, TRUNCATE and DESCRIBE stay out because SQLite lacks them.

steps.title: DML: adding, changing and removing rows
steps.reason: A DELETE leaves rows a second SELECT reads back, and the page's own case, two rows answering to ticket 1, makes the named mistakes fail: WHERE ticket_id = 1 alone removes both, and no WHERE removes every ticket. The task is the duplicate on tickets, a sibling of the exercise's delete_sql on loans, not that function.

steps.title: DQL: reading rows with SELECT
steps.reason: A SELECT's column list, its WHERE on one column and its AS aliases show up as the rows and the column names a check reads from the cursor. SELECT * and a list without AS give the wrong headings, and a missing WHERE returns all six tickets; everything used runs unchanged on SQLite 3.39.

steps.title: DCL: who may run what
steps.reason: CREATE USER, GRANT, REVOKE, SHOW GRANTS and the ERROR 1142 refusal belong to MySQL's account system, which SQLite does not have, so the step stays none until ix-sql (D-0062) lands. The page's slips, a missing host part and ON ticket_desk without .*, only fail against a MySQL server.

steps.title: TCL: changes that land or vanish together
steps.reason: The step's point is START TRANSACTION, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT and autocommit typed at the mysql client, and the implicit commit a CREATE TABLE causes; SQLite has no START TRANSACTION and does not commit on DDL, so the bar rules it out. A transaction is also several statements, and a task here is one.

steps.title: The five sublanguages side by side
steps.reason: The step sorts statements into five groups, which the page itself calls a teaching convention, and which ones ROLLBACK can undo; no statement's rows show that sorting, so the bar's first rule rules it out. The Check yourself question on naming the groups practises it aloud.

steps.title: Getting ready for your interview, part 2
steps.reason: The step teaches the shape of a spoken answer (definition, example, limit), practised aloud with a partner, which no check can see. Its runnable block compares DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP, and TRUNCATE does not exist in SQLite; DELETE and DROP are already practised in t1 and t2.

tasks.title: DDL
tasks.idea: The reader writes one DROP statement that removes the scratch_notes table and can be run again safely, as a clean-up script needs. The setup builds customers, agents and tickets with their rows plus scratch_notes with two notes, runs the statement, and runs it a second time. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scratch_notes; is the shape.
checks: After the statement, scratch_notes no longer exists, read back from sqlite_master; DELETE FROM scratch_notes empties the table but keeps it and fails.
Running the same statement a second time, with the table already gone, raises no error; a plain DROP TABLE scratch_notes fails here, as the second DROP on the page does.
The tickets table still holds its six rows, so a DROP that names the wrong table fails.
tasks.q: The checks build the desk's customers, agents and tickets tables with their rows, plus a scratch_notes table holding two notes. Write one DDL statement that removes the scratch_notes table itself, its definition and its rows, and that a clean-up script can run a second time without an error once the table is gone. Type the statement between the triple quotes; the checks run it, then run it again. Afterwards the database holds the tables customers, agents and tickets and no scratch_notes, and the second run reports no error.
tasks.starter:
QUERY = """
-- remove scratch_notes so the statement can run twice
"""
tasks.tests:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
conn.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id INT,
    name VARCHAR(100),
    email VARCHAR(255),
    country CHAR(2),
    monthly_fee DECIMAL(8,2)
);
CREATE TABLE agents (
    agent_id INT,
    name VARCHAR(50),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);
CREATE TABLE tickets (
    ticket_id INT,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    priority VARCHAR(10),
    status VARCHAR(10),
    customer_id INT,
    agent_id INT,
    opened_at DATETIME,
    closed_at DATETIME
);
INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, name, email, country, monthly_fee)
VALUES (1, 'Dana Whitfield', 'dana@example.com', 'CA', 49.00),
       (2, 'Ravi Patel', 'ravi@example.com', 'CA', 199.00),
       (3, 'Mei Chen', 'mei@example.com', 'US', 0.00),
       (4, 'Omar Haddad', 'omar@example.com', 'GB', 49.00);
INSERT INTO agents (agent_id, name, email)
VALUES (1, 'Priya', 'priya@desk.example'),
       (2, 'Marco', 'marco@desk.example'),
       (3, 'Sam', 'sam@desk.example'),
       (4, 'Lee', 'lee@desk.example');
INSERT INTO tickets (ticket_id, title, priority, status, customer_id, agent_id, opened_at, closed_at)
VALUES (1, 'Login page returns 500', 'high', 'closed', 1, NULL, '2026-10-18 08:00:00', '2026-10-18 11:00:00'),
       (2, 'Invoice PDF is blank', 'normal', 'closed', 2, NULL, '2026-10-17 12:00:00', '2026-10-18 18:00:00'),
       (3, 'Typo on pricing page', 'normal', 'closed', 1, NULL, '2026-10-18 18:00:00', '2026-10-19 04:00:00'),
       (4, 'Checkout button frozen', 'high', 'assigned', 3, 1, '2026-10-19 08:00:00', NULL),
       (5, 'Export is missing rows', 'normal', 'assigned', 2, 2, '2026-10-18 12:00:00', NULL),
       (6, 'Add a dark mode', 'low', 'open', 3, NULL, '2026-10-19 12:00:00', NULL);
CREATE TABLE scratch_notes (
    note_id INT,
    body VARCHAR(50)
);
INSERT INTO scratch_notes VALUES (1, 'call back'), (2, 'refund sent');
""")
cur = conn.execute(QUERY)
rows = cur.fetchall()
assert conn.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'scratch_notes'").fetchall() == [], "scratch_notes is gone as a table, not just emptied"
assert not raises(sqlite3.Error, conn.execute, QUERY), "a second run, with scratch_notes already gone, raises no error"
assert [r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name != 'scratch_notes' ORDER BY name")] == ["agents", "customers", "tickets"], "customers, agents and tickets are all still there"

tasks.title: DML
tasks.idea: The setup loads the six desk tickets plus the second ticket 1 from the page, an open copy of the closed one. The reader writes one DELETE that removes only the open duplicate: DELETE FROM tickets WHERE ticket_id = 1 AND status = 'open';. Afterwards one ticket 1 remains, the closed one.
checks: Exactly one row is removed, read from conn.total_changes; DELETE FROM tickets WHERE ticket_id = 1 removes both copies and fails.
One row with ticket_id 1 remains and its status is 'closed'; a condition on status = 'closed' removes the wrong copy and fails.
Tickets 2 to 6 are all still there; a DELETE with no WHERE removes every ticket and fails.
tasks.q: The checks load the six desk tickets into tickets (columns ticket_id, title, priority, status, customer_id, agent_id, opened_at, closed_at) plus the second ticket 1 from the DELETE section above: the same title with status 'open', next to the original whose status is 'closed'. Write one DELETE that removes only the open copy of ticket 1. Afterwards one row has ticket_id 1, the closed one, and tickets 2 to 6 are untouched. Type the statement between the triple quotes.
tasks.starter:
QUERY = """
-- remove the open copy of ticket 1 and nothing else
"""
tasks.tests:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
conn.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE tickets (
    ticket_id INT,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    priority VARCHAR(10),
    status VARCHAR(10),
    customer_id INT,
    agent_id INT,
    opened_at DATETIME,
    closed_at DATETIME
);
INSERT INTO tickets (ticket_id, title, priority, status, customer_id, agent_id, opened_at, closed_at)
VALUES (1, 'Login page returns 500', 'high', 'closed', 1, NULL, '2026-10-18 08:00:00', '2026-10-18 11:00:00'),
       (2, 'Invoice PDF is blank', 'normal', 'closed', 2, NULL, '2026-10-17 12:00:00', '2026-10-18 18:00:00'),
       (3, 'Typo on pricing page', 'normal', 'closed', 1, NULL, '2026-10-18 18:00:00', '2026-10-19 04:00:00'),
       (4, 'Checkout button frozen', 'high', 'assigned', 3, 1, '2026-10-19 08:00:00', NULL),
       (5, 'Export is missing rows', 'normal', 'assigned', 2, 2, '2026-10-18 12:00:00', NULL),
       (6, 'Add a dark mode', 'low', 'open', 3, NULL, '2026-10-19 12:00:00', NULL);
INSERT INTO tickets (ticket_id, title, priority, status, customer_id, agent_id, opened_at, closed_at)
VALUES (1, 'Login page returns 500', 'high', 'open', 1, NULL, '2026-10-20 09:00:00', NULL);
""")
before = conn.total_changes
cur = conn.execute(QUERY)
rows = cur.fetchall()
assert conn.total_changes - before == 1, "removes exactly one row"
assert conn.execute("SELECT status FROM tickets WHERE ticket_id = 1").fetchall() == [("closed",)], "the one ticket 1 left is the closed one"
assert conn.execute("SELECT ticket_id FROM tickets WHERE ticket_id > 1 ORDER BY ticket_id").fetchall() == [(2,), (3,), (4,), (5,), (6,)], "tickets 2 to 6 are all still there"

tasks.title: DQL
tasks.idea: The reader writes one SELECT that returns the tickets with status 'assigned', showing ticket_id under the heading id and title under the heading summary, in that order. On the seeded desk it returns (4, 'Checkout button frozen') and (5, 'Export is missing rows').
checks: The result columns are named id and summary, in that order; SELECT * and a column list without AS give other headings and fail.
The rows are exactly tickets 4 and 5 with their titles, compared sorted; leaving out WHERE returns all six tickets and fails.
Each row holds two values, the id before the title; a list written title first fails.
tasks.q: The checks load the six desk tickets into tickets (columns ticket_id, title, priority, status, customer_id, agent_id, opened_at, closed_at). Write one SELECT that returns the tickets whose status is 'assigned', with two result columns: ticket_id under the heading id, then title under the heading summary. AS changes only the headings of the result, not the table. On these rows it returns (4, 'Checkout button frozen') and (5, 'Export is missing rows'), in any order. Type the statement between the triple quotes.
tasks.starter:
QUERY = """
-- the assigned tickets as id and summary
"""
tasks.tests:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
conn.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE tickets (
    ticket_id INT,
    title VARCHAR(200),
    priority VARCHAR(10),
    status VARCHAR(10),
    customer_id INT,
    agent_id INT,
    opened_at DATETIME,
    closed_at DATETIME
);
INSERT INTO tickets (ticket_id, title, priority, status, customer_id, agent_id, opened_at, closed_at)
VALUES (1, 'Login page returns 500', 'high', 'closed', 1, NULL, '2026-10-18 08:00:00', '2026-10-18 11:00:00'),
       (2, 'Invoice PDF is blank', 'normal', 'closed', 2, NULL, '2026-10-17 12:00:00', '2026-10-18 18:00:00'),
       (3, 'Typo on pricing page', 'normal', 'closed', 1, NULL, '2026-10-18 18:00:00', '2026-10-19 04:00:00'),
       (4, 'Checkout button frozen', 'high', 'assigned', 3, 1, '2026-10-19 08:00:00', NULL),
       (5, 'Export is missing rows', 'normal', 'assigned', 2, 2, '2026-10-18 12:00:00', NULL),
       (6, 'Add a dark mode', 'low', 'open', 3, NULL, '2026-10-19 12:00:00', NULL);
""")
cur = conn.execute(QUERY)
rows = cur.fetchall()
assert [c[0] for c in cur.description] == ["id", "summary"], "the result columns are headed id and summary, in that order"
assert sorted(rows) == [(4, "Checkout button frozen"), (5, "Export is missing rows")], "returns the two assigned tickets and no others"
assert all(len(r) == 2 and isinstance(r[0], int) and isinstance(r[1], str) for r in rows), "each row holds two values, the ticket id before the title"
